rationale: The buyer is clear and well-funded — Salesforce admins and support-ops managers at B2B companies are a named role with real budget, and the Salesforce AppExchange ecosystem has demonstrated high willingness to pay for point solutions. However, the solution is not buildable as a simple Claude + Stripe setup: it requires a Salesforce-connected app, Apex triggers or Flow customisation, and AppExchange security review — all of which exceed standard factory tooling and demand platform-specific engineering. Operational autonomy is low because any fix must live inside each customer's Salesforce org, making per-customer setup manual. Both `buildability_with_ai` (4) and `operational_autonomy` (4) fail build gates, capping stage at validate.
solution_plan: The micro-service would be a Salesforce Email-to-Case deduplication tool — likely a managed package or a guided configuration recipe — that detects when a single inbound email spawns multiple cases and suppresses or merges duplicates automatically. Building it requires native Salesforce skills (Apex, Flow, or connected-app APIs) that go beyond what the Claude factory can generate and ship without a Salesforce developer partner; this is not a Claude-prompt-plus-landing-page problem. If Youval has or can recruit a Salesforce ISV partner, validation is worth running: reach out to 20–30 Salesforce admins via Salesforce StackExchange, Trailblazer Community, and LinkedIn with a 'would you pay $X/mo for a one-click fix?' message (all outreach approved before sending). Realistically, a solo non-technical operator cannot build and maintain this without either a Salesforce-native developer or an existing AppExchange product to white-label. Recommend validating demand only and parking build until a technical co-builder is identified.
notes: Failing build gates: operational_autonomy (4 < 7 min), buildability_with_ai (4 < 6 min). Core constraint is Salesforce platform lock-in — solution must live inside each customer's org.
